title: OTEL + Grafana Terraform refactor proposal for private deployments
content:
Purpose and scope:

This is a working proposal to refactor the Terraform modules and upgrade plan for observability in Redwood private deployments (VPC + on-prem installs). Focus is on standardizing provisioning for:
- OpenTelemetry Collector (metrics + traces)
- Prometheus stack (scraping + local TSDB +/- long-term storage)
- Grafana (dashboards, provisioning)
- Log shipping (Vector or Fluent Bit to remote/archives)

Goals:
- Single, composable Terraform module set that can be consumed by both our VPC and on-prem installers
- Clear separation of infra, app manifests, and secrets (KMS/HSM integration where available)
- Minimal blast radius for upgrades (can upgrade OTEL or Prometheus independently)
- Strong testing checklist + rollback plan for upgrade windows
- Improve defaults for retention/cost tradeoffs and make them configurable per-customer

High-level design notes:
- Terraform modules: propose a small module surface: observability/core, observability/prometheus, observability/grafana, observability/log-collector.
  - observability/core: sets up namespace, service accounts, network ACLs, base config map, bootstrap TLS secrets (or references to KMS), optional remote-write credentials.
  - observability/prometheus: installs Prometheus (k8s manifest or Helm release), exposes Service/Ingress for internal use, configures scrape jobs, retention, persistence class. Outputs: prometheus_service_name, prometheus_endpoint, rule_group_configmap_name.
  - observability/grafana: installs Grafana with provisioning config (dashboards + datasources). Supports either internal admin password OR external SSO integration (OIDC).
  - observability/log-collector: installs Vector/FluentBit + LogForwarder config. Supports local disk buffer + remote archive to S3-compatible storage.

Why separate modules?
- Customers may want only metrics, or only logs, or want to run Prometheus outside k8s. Small modules reduce coupling and make upgrades less risky.

Terraform implementation details / conventions:
- Remote state: require per-environment remote state (S3/GCS + locking). Workspaces should be avoided for prod; prefer separate state per customer/deployment.
- Module input conventions: prefix all inputs with "observability_" to avoid collisions (e.g. observability_retention_days).
- Version pinning: provider and helm chart versions must be explicit. Enforce with CI tfsec/terraform fmt and lock file.
- Secrets: no plaintext secrets in TF. All sensitive values are retrieved from KMS or passed as data from an external secrets store (Vault) and injected into k8s as sealed secrets. TF module should accept a sealedsecret name or reference.
- Naming: resources should be suffixed with a short id variable (var.deployment_shortname) to avoid long names in on-prem.

Prometheus specifics:
- Default retention: 15d for standard customers, configurable via observability_retention_days. Recommend 90d only for Dedicated customers with extra storage commit.
- Storage: prefer PVC with storage class set by module consumer. For long-term storage we provision Thanos sidecar or remote_write to customer's long-term TSDB (Cortex/VM/Hosted). Module supports an optional thanos block.
- Scrape config: modules generate a base scrape config and append job fragments via k8s configmap. CI/Test harness will validate that the generated scrape config does not permit open endpoints.
- Rule management: store Prometheus rules as files in git (repo: infra-observability-rules). Terraform will create a ConfigMap referencing the rule files.

OpenTelemetry Collector:
- Deploy as a deployment/daemonset (configurable). Collector receives metrics/traces from app pods (via sidecar or node exporter) and exports to Prometheus (metrics -> Prometheus remote_write) and to tracing backends (Jaeger/OTLP).
- For private deployments the collector will be configured to: 1) receive OTLP via gRPC 2) batch + retry windows tuned for low-bandwidth environments 3) optionally buffer to disk.
- Config management: collector config should be templatized and rendered with terraform-local-file or k8s_manifest. Keep a small set of supported exporter backends.

Logs shipping:
- Recommend Vector as the default (smaller footprint than Fluentd, strong backpressure guarantees). Vector will tail logs, transform (remove PII fields), and send to either customer's ELK/Hosted endpoint or to S3/Minio archive.
- Buffering: enable local disk buffer with configurable max_bytes and max_age. For air-gapped installs ensure archive -> on-prem object store.

Upgrade plan (high level):
1) Pre-upgrade validation:
   - Validate terraform plan in CI with a dry-run environment (staging).
   - Run linting against OTEL/Prometheus configs (promtool check-rules, otelconfig validator).
   - Export current Prometheus TSDB snapshot (if possible) and back up Grafana DB.
2) Canary rollout:
   - For k8s installs: roll out new OTEL Collector as new deployment with canary label; route 10% traffic for 48h; check ingestion rates, CPU, memory, errors.
   - For Prometheus: deploy new Prometheus instance configured to read same targets (read-only) and compare metrics via query diffs.
3) Full rollout and verification:
   - Increase rollout gradually and monitor key SLOs (ingestion completeness, alert count, query latency).
   - Post-upgrade: run validation queries and smoke dashboards (list included below).
4) Rollback strategy:
   - Have Terraform apply that can pin old image/tag and redeploy old manifests. Keep DB snapshots so Prometheus can be reattached.

Testing checklist (must be automated where possible):
- Terraform plan validation and unit tests for modules (terratest)
- Prometheus rule syntax checks, and a small test harness that runs a set of queries against the new Prometheus and the baseline to detect diffs > threshold.
- Grafana provisioning smoke: ensure datasources load and dashboards render without missing metrics.
- OTEL: sample traces forwarded and appear in tracing backend; check spans count and durations.
- Logs: sample log sent -> validate retention and archive.

Runbook snippets (for on-call):
- Symptom: Prometheus scrape errors spike -> quick checks:
  - kubectl get pods -n observability | grep prometheus
  - kubectl logs prometheus-pod -n observability | tail 200
  - promtool check-config /etc/prometheus/prometheus.yml
  - If PVC pressure: check DF on node and check storageclass reclaim policy.
- Symptom: OTEL collector high restart count -> check collector config for invalid exporter endpoint or buffer size.

Network & security considerations:
- Required ports (internal-only):
  - Prometheus scrape: TCP 9090 (in-cluster) or 9100 for node-exporter
  - OTLP gRPC: 4317 (collector)
  - Grafana: 3000 internal (or customer-specified LB port)
- ACLs: TF module will create security group rules that are deny-by-default and only open listed source CIDRs.
- Encryption: enable TLS for Grafana and collector endpoints. Secrets should reference customer's KMS or Vault.
- Audit logs: enable k8s audit policy snippet and ship to log archive.

Outstanding questions / decision points:
- Vector vs Fluent Bit: Vector is preferred but some customers require Fluent Bit compatibility. Module should support both via a flag.
- Long-term metrics: Thanos vs external remote_write. Decide recommended default for Redwood-managed Dedicated customers.
- Grafana provisioning: do we ship curated Redwood dashboards by default? (Proposal: include a minimal set and make heavier dashboards opt-in.)

Backward compatibility & migration notes:
- Old installs used a monolithic observability helm chart. Migration will create the new resources side-by-side and move scrape targets. Ensure service discovery labels preserved.
- For customers with existing Prometheus TSDB, attach Thanos sidecar for read-only comparisons before switching writers.

Implementation timeline (rough):
- Week 0-2: implement observability/core and prometheus modules, basic tests
- Week 3-4: grafana + log-collector modules, CI integration, and terratest scaffolding
- Week 5: internal canary on staging customer, gather telemetry and iterate
- Week 6-8: beta with 2 customers (one VPC, one on-prem air-gapped)
- Week 9+: GA + docs + runbooks

Files to add to repo (infra-observability):
- modules/observability/core/main.tf + variables + outputs
- modules/observability/prometheus/helm-values.yaml + helpers for scrape generation
- modules/observability/grafana/provisioning/dashboards
- modules/observability/log-collector/vector/configs/*
- test/terratest/* integration tests
- docs/private-deployments/upgrade-playbook.md (rendered from this doc)

Quick TODOs (short-term):
- [ ] Finalize module input names and defaults (open PR: GH#87)
- [ ] Add promtool + otel config unit tests to CI
- [ ] Create a migration checklist for customers with existing Prometheus instances
- [ ] Decide on default long-term metrics solution (Thanos vs remote_write)

Notes to reviewers:
- This is intentionally prescriptive in module boundaries to reduce coupling; feedback welcome if we should combine grafana+prometheus in a single module for simpler installs.
- Please comment on recommended defaults for retention and what the minimal required exporter backends should be.

Attachments (planned): links to sample TF variable docs, example OTEL config fragments, and sample Vector pipelines - will add as separate files in repo.

End of proposal.
